predecessors.name: Duchy of Naples
predecessors.text: 'Sergius IV of Naples gave the town and vicinity of Aversa as a county to Ranulf' (County of Aversa); Cliopatria's 1034 shape is that county

successors.name: Kingdom of Sicily
successors.text: the whole Norman realm of Roger II (Sicily, Calabria, Apulia and the duchy lands), crowned king at Palermo on Christmas Day 1130; Capua and Naples are not yet in it

rulers.name: Roger II
rulers.title: Duke of Apulia and Calabria, Count of Sicily

ledger.x: 1030: Ranulf becomes Count of Aversa.
1038: Ranulf invades Capua.
1041: the Normans fight the Byzantines for Apulia.
1043: the County of Apulia is founded.
1044: the conquest of Calabria begins.
1057: Richard besieges Capua.
1058: Richard takes Capua and the Aversa lands leave this state.
1058: the siege of Capua ends with Richard and Jordan as princes.
1059: the county becomes a duchy.
1060: Reggio and Calabria.
1060: the Calabrian contest is settled with the fall of Reggio.
1061: Messina, the first permanent conquest in Sicily.
1061: the invasion of Sicily.
1071: Bari surrenders.
1071: the Byzantine presence in southern Italy ends.
1072: Palermo falls.
1077: Salerno.
1078: the capital moves from Melfi to Salerno.
1078: Guiscard is appointed to Benevento.
1081: Guiscard gives Benevento up.
1085: the rest of Sicily outside the south-eastern corner, as Cliopatria draws it.

1091: Malta. 'In 1091, Roger invaded Malta and subdued the walled city of Mdina.' The County of Sicily page: the conquest 'was begun later that year' and completed in 1127, when 'the Arab administration of the island was expelled'. Cliopatria draws Malta from 1094.
1091: Noto falls and Sicily is complete.
1091: the contest for Sicily ends.
1127: Palermo becomes the capital of the united realm.
1127: Roger II inherits the mainland duchy.
1128: Honorius II invests Roger as duke.
1130: Roger II is crowned king of Sicily at Palermo.

wars.name: Norman-Byzantine war in Apulia and Calabria
wars.outcome: Norman victory: Melfi and Apulia held from 1042-1043, Reggio taken in 1060, Bari in April 1071 'ending the Byzantine presence in southern Italy'.

wars.name: Battle of Civitate
wars.outcome: Norman victory on 18 June 1053 over 'the combined forces of the pope and the Holy Roman Empire'; 'the Normans destroyed the papal army and captured Leo IX, imprisoning him in Benevento'.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Capua
wars.outcome: Richard besieged the town in 1057 and, with Jordan, took the princely title in 1058; the counts of Aversa became princes of Capua.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Sicily
wars.outcome: Norman victory: Messina besieged May 1061, Palermo entered 7 January 1072, Noto fell in February 1091 and 'the conquest of Sicily was complete'; Malta invaded in 1091.

wars.name: Norman conquest of the Principality of Salerno
wars.outcome: Salerno submitted on 13 December 1076 and its citadel fell in May 1077; the lands were added to the Duchy of Apulia and Calabria.

certainty.note: Every frontier of the century of conquest is approximate: the counties and the duchy grew by campaigns and fiefs, not by surveyed lines.
